text: There's a fire on your stove... you might not be able to see.
Do you know what happens when your stove runs on hydrogen?
Hydrogen is the clean fuel everyone's betting on. It burns into... water.
But a pure hydrogen flame can be almost invisible.
So why do some look bright orange? Here's the weird part.
It's salt. Sea salt, blowing in from the ocean.
Scientists in Australia watched hydrogen burners for two weeks. Same settings, every single day.
The orange glow changed by more than twenty-eight times... just because of the wind.
Wind from the sea? Bright flame. Wind from inland? Barely there.
And a hydrogen cooktop gave off less light than a normal gas stove... even on a good day.
Future hydrogen stoves can't count on your eyes.
They'll need sensors that see heat and ultraviolet light... so nobody touches a fire they can't see.
Would you cook on a flame you can't see?
